blockers.description: UNDECLARED + UNPINNED non-interactive behaviour delta on the MEDIUM-3 escaped spelling under --parser combinator, and three COMMITTED artifacts that assert the opposite. The slot's central latency claim — that `echo \<<EOF` is observable only at a terminal, so a -c pin would be green-on-base — is FALSE for the combinator on all three non-interactive channels. Brief §7 ("an unpinned improvement is still a bounce") applies, and this is the THIRD occurrence of the R7-B / R11-B class the slot was already bounced for twice (R11-B: "a delta is ALL-CHANNEL until the identity instrument proves otherwise"). ROOT CAUSE is the chartered fix itself: at base the session's regex opened a phantom heredoc so the following physical lines joined ONE buffer, and the combinator stamps every top-level statement with that buffer's start line (the 2.2 carry, which I verified is UNTOUCHED and base-identical); at tip each line is its own buffer, so line numbers become correct. It moves psh TOWARD bash — it just is not declared, not pinned, and is contradicted in shipped text. The dev's identity instrument missed it because its `escaped_lt.in` case is `echo \<<EOF` + `echo MARK""ER`, whose follow-up line emits NO diagnostic: the exposing axis ("does the swallowed line emit a line-numbered diagnostic") is unvaried across the whole 22-case / 132-row corpus, which reports escaped_lt IDENTICAL. REMEDY: re-declare the escaped spelling honestly (rd = latent; combinator = all-channel), add an inputs/ case whose follow-up lines produce diagnostics, re-run base_tip_identity.py, pin the non-interactive half per channel/parser, and correct the three committed texts.
